name: tabular_mlflow
title: An MLflow-tracked credit-risk sweep whose every logged number is computed wrongly
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-tabular: the experiment-tracking shape, and the two metric-argument defects MLV305 / MLV306 exist for

expected.defect: the scaler already fitted on the training half is re-fitted on the held-out half
expected.why: the test features are standardised by their own mean and variance, so the model is scored on a distribution it was never trained on

expected.defect: roc_auc_score is handed model.predict(...) output, which is a hard 0/1 label
expected.why: the ROC curve then has two points, so the number logged as roc_auc is balanced accuracy wearing an AUC label, and it is the number the sweep is ranked on

expected.defect: accuracy_score is handed the raw probability column rather than a decision
expected.why: a continuous vector is compared for equality against 0/1 labels, so the logged accuracy is roughly zero whatever the model does

forbidden.why: the first fit at line 44 is on train_x, after the split at line 40 - the correct order; the defect in this file is the second fit, which is MLV102's
there is no cross-validation call in this project
there is no timestamp in this project
np.random.seed is called at line 74 and the split and the forest both carry random_state=SEED
f1_score is a class metric and `decisions` is what it should be given; only the roc_auc_score call above it is the ranking-metric defect
there is no torch in this project

notes: MLV117 (train_test_split without stratify=) is catalogued but not implemented, so it cannot carry a forbidden label; for the record, in experiment.py: the split passes stratify=labels
